landing.decisionsTitle: What we chose, and what it costs

prepare.chose: We prepare the GST/QST return: the figures, line by line, with the working papers.
prepare.refused: Filing in your name, or promising electronic transmission.
prepare.because: You stay the one who signs; the figures come from your ledger, never from a guess.
prepare.cost: You file it yourself, with your figures in hand.

canada.chose: Data in Canada, encrypted at rest, consent per purpose (Loi 25).
canada.refused: Pre-ticked consent, data across the border, files kept forever.
canada.because: A client's file is theirs; the law of Québec says so since 2023.
canada.cost: Erasing a client keeps the invoices (six years, tax law) but nothing personal.

pos.chose: Bookings, invoices and taxes first; the point of sale later.
pos.refused: Restaurants and bars, which must bill through a certified SRM.
pos.because: A till done half-right is worse than none.
pos.cost: No payment terminal yet: payments are recorded, not processed.

landing.promise: I build your shop's books, line by line, and I never file anything without you.

points: Two appointments of one person never overlap — the database itself refuses it.
A cancelled appointment frees its slot at once.

invoice.title: GST 5 %, QST 9.975 %, to the cent
invoice.lead: Taxes computed once on the taxable subtotal, rounded half up — zero-rated bread stays at zero, a small supplier charges nothing.
points: Every invoice posts its GST and QST to an append-only ledger; the database checks they add up.
A correction is a credit note, never an edit.
“Prepare my tax return” lays out the FPZ-500 figures with their sources — assisted by an Orazaka Studio, checked against your ledger, filed by you.

privacy.title: Your clients' files, governed

points: Consent per purpose (the service, reminders, marketing), never pre-ticked, every decision kept.
Erasure blanks every personal field and keeps the invoices the tax law requires.
Data in Canada, encrypted at rest.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Akinaza is in development: only the accounts our team creates can sign in. A shop's data — its clients, appointments, invoices and tax ledger — is kept in Akinaza's database in Canada, encrypted at rest, visible to that shop only. Client consent is recorded per purpose (Loi 25) and can be withdrawn; a client's personal information can be erased, while the invoices tax law requires are kept. When a merchant asks to prepare a tax return, the period's ledger is sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's engine, over HTTPS; nothing is filed or transmitted to any government. Nothing is sold or shared. To ask a question or have your data removed, use the contact form.
